endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Vendor/Solution remediation — Document the specific failure and formally request the vendor/developer address it before wider deployment proceeds, with a defined timeline and re-validation criteria.

endorsements.title: Adoption of AI in Healthcare Delivery Systems: Early Applications and Impacts
endorsements.quote: While some of these functional areas have well-defined, industry standard metrics, others will likely require focused measurement approaches to identify how AI-enabled solutions should scale across an enterprise, as well as approaches to pricing that align with value creation.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Responsible AI checkpoints are crucial, both before and after an AI system is in use (during silent deployment and pilot stages, then again at regular intervals during general deployment).

endorsements.title: Implementation of artificial intelligence in thoracic imaging-a what, how, and why guide from the European Society of Thoracic Imaging (ESTI)
endorsements.quote: The predefined metrics which need to be included in the approval for each algorithm should be defined by radiologists working with clinicians who have knowledge of the patient pathway and the significance of each step should be included, in order to safeguard patient care.

endorsements.title: AI-driven high-risk pregnancy prediction: balancing early detection, anxiety, and discrimination in digital public health
endorsements.quote: Pilots should pair subgroup calibration with perinatal-anxiety measures (e.g., Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale–Anxiety subscale/Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scale trajectories) and pre-specified stop rules before scale-up.

endorsements.title: AI-Assisted Formative Assessment in Clinical Education: From Algorithms to Agency
endorsements.quote: Before scaling, local pilots should prespecify a small evaluation set, such as learner participation, quality of action plans, change between repeated attempts, quality of dialogue between faculty and learners, learner trust, faculty time burden, equity of access, and unintended effects on assessment culture.

endorsements.title: From prediction to practice: artificial intelligence as an enabling layer in liver transplant care - reflections on ILTS 2025
endorsements.quote: Pilot clinical trials that examine AI-augmented decision support for immunosuppression dosing, such as the AIIM trial, should incorporate predefined safety thresholds and real-time monitoring of adverse events.

endorsements.title: Equity-centred, nurse-led implementation of artificial intelligence in community maternal and child health nursing: a conceptual framework for low-resource settings
endorsements.quote: Locally validated model with equity-stratified performance audit; consent and governance processes in place; alternative access pathway available for excluded groups.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether predefined pilot thresholds and a formal decision gate change scaling decisions or patient outcomes, and no study documents how often tools scale without evidence of pilot success. Eight sources endorse the practice, mostly commentaries and two frameworks, so the recommendation currently rests on expert agreement.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Of eight endorsements, two are frameworks, one is guidance, and five are commentaries. Agreement across sources reflects expert opinion, which GRADE does not treat as evidence of effect, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

Several endorsers ask for prespecified stop rules, safety thresholds, and real-time adverse event monitoring during pilots, which would give a committee a defined point to halt a tool before wider exposure. Without studies, it remains unknown whether such gates catch failures that informal review would miss, or how often thresholds are set too loosely to trigger.

Two endorsers call for subgroup calibration and equity-stratified performance audits as part of pilot criteria, and one addresses low-resource community settings. These sources describe what thresholds should contain, but no study shows that stratified gates detect or prevent performance gaps in Medicaid, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy groups.

One guidance source states that some functional areas lack standard metrics and will need focused measurement approaches before enterprise scaling. This suggests that defining thresholds may require local analytic work for each tool. No study reports the staff time, cost, or delay that a formal decision gate adds to deployment.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares deployments governed by predefined success, failure, and responsible AI thresholds with deployments scaled through informal judgment. Useful studies would measure how often gates lead to halting or remediation, whether halted tools would have caused harm, the time and staff cost of the gate, and whether subgroup-stratified thresholds change decisions.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Two endorsements recommend equity-stratified audits and one addresses low-resource settings, but whether decision gates protect these groups remains untested.
